battle.name: 美國福爾摩沙遠征
battle.brief: 1867年6月13日，美國分艦隊少將貝爾率兩艘戰艦，護送181名水兵與海軍陸戰隊員在恆春半島登岸，遠征琅嶠十八社排灣族以報羅發號沉船之仇。縱隊在叢林行軍約六小時，屢遭山頭火槍伏擊，少校麥肯齊中彈陣亡，餘眾因酷熱撤回艦上，遠征以撤退收場。卡面加特林機槍此時剛入美軍序列，並未發射。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 交戰的一方是美國海軍東印度分艦隊，另一方是臺灣南部琅嶠十八社（斯卡羅）的排灣族各部落，中間夾着清廷的地方官僚。美國一方由分艦隊司令少將亨利·H·貝爾（Henry H. Bell）指揮，旗艦是蒸汽巡洋艦「哈特福」號（USS Hartford），同行者為木殼螺旋槳巡洋艦「懷俄明」號（USS Wyoming）；在此之前另有新服役的炮艇「阿休埃洛特」號（USS Ashuelot）奉命赴臺查案。登陸部隊共181名軍官、水兵與海軍陸戰隊員，灘頭指揮官是「哈特福」號中校喬治·E·貝爾納普（George E. Belknap），副手為海軍少校亞歷山大·史密德·麥肯齊（Alexander Slidell MacKenzie），陸戰隊則由詹姆斯·福尼（James Forney）上尉率領。對面沒有國家編制，只以部落為單位：龜仔甪社（Kulaljuc，今社頂部落）與豬朥束社是作戰主體，總頭目卓杞篤（Tok-a-Tok，約1817年至1874年在世）居中調度，各社另有獵首與戰士，中文史料另列頭目巴耶林。清廷方面，臺灣隸屬福建，1867年歸閩浙總督統轄，地方上由臺灣鎮總兵劉明燈、臺灣兵備道吳大廷、臺灣府知府葉宗元分掌兵備、行政與海防；美方在廈門的領事李仙得（C. W. Le Gendre）則在美方、清廷與原住民三方之間穿針引線。
countriesEn: One side was the United States Navy East India Station, the other the Paiwan villages of the eighteen communities of Niaosong (Langjiao) in southern Taiwan, the Skaroo confederacy, with the Qing local bureaucracy wedged between them. The American side was commanded by Rear Admiral Henry H. Bell, commander of the East India Station, with the steam frigate USS Hartford as his flagship and the wooden screw sloop of war USS Wyoming in company; before them the newly commissioned gunboat USS Ashuelot had been sent to the island to investigate. The landing force numbered 181 officers, sailors and marines. The beach commander was Lieutenant Commander George E. Belknap of the Hartford, seconded by Lieutenant Commander Alexander Slidell MacKenzie, while the marines were led by Captain James Forney. The enemy had no state organisation and fought village by village: the communities of Kulaljuc (Kulaljuc, today She Ding) and the nearby Zhu-lao-shu were the actual combatants, with the confederacy head Tok-a-Tok (c. 1817 - 1874) coordinating between them and each village supplying its own hunting leaders and warriors; the Chinese records additionally name a headman called Payelin. On the Qing side Taiwan belonged to Fujian and in 1867 fell under the governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, while in the island itself the Taiwan garrison commander Liu Mingdeng, the Taiwan circuit intendant Wu Dating and the prefect of Taiwan Yeh Zongyuan divided the military, civil and coastal-defence portfolios. The American consul at Xiamen, C. W. Le Gendre, worked as the go-between for the Americans, the Qing court and the aboriginal communities.
people: 關鍵人物集中在三處。艦上方面，東印度分艦隊少將亨利·H·貝爾拍板用兵；奉命赴臺調查的「阿休埃洛特」號炮艇指揮官約翰·費比傑（John C. Febiger）是最早到達現場的美方人員；領事李仙得自1867年4月18日起在臺灣府嘗試與排灣族直接聯絡，四月間屢屢碰壁，才使華盛頓轉而決定出兵；駐華公使蒲安臣（Anson Burlingame）獲悉事件後把本案交由李仙得處理。登陸當日，貝爾納普中校統帶一隊，麥肯齊少校率另一隊。麥肯齊出身美國海軍世家，父親蘭納爾·斯萊德爾·麥肯齊是作家兼外交官，他本人在1867年6月13日最後一次接觸中被排灣族戰士的一次齊射擊中重傷不治，成為這場遠征中唯一的美方陣亡者。另一端的總頭目卓杞篤是琅嶠十八社的實際決策者，1867年10月10日在琅嶠與清方、美方訂下「南岬之盟」，1869年2月28日又邀集李仙得把口頭約定寫成書面備忘錄。清廷官員中，臺灣鎮總兵劉明燈率兵五百員進駐車城一帶，臺灣兵備道吳大廷與臺灣府知府葉宗元則在設砲臺、設官一事上持反對立場。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities divide into three groups. Ashore of the ships: Rear Admiral Henry H. Bell of the East India Station decided on the use of force; Commander John C. Febiger of the gunboat USS Ashuelot, sent to the island to investigate, was the first American on the spot; Consul C. W. Le Gendre had been trying since 18 April 1867, from the prefectural city of Taiwan, to open direct contact with the Paiwan, and after repeated rebuffs it was his failure that turned Washington toward military action; Anson Burlingame, the American minister to China, took the case from the British legation and handed it to Le Gendre. On the day of the landing Lieutenant Commander Belknap led one column and Lieutenant Commander MacKenzie the other. MacKenzie came from a naval family: his father, Ranald Slidell Mackenzie, was an author and diplomat, and the son himself was mortally wounded in the last contact of 13 June 1867 by a single musket volley fired by the Paiwan warriors, becoming the only American officer killed in the expedition. At the other end, the confederacy head Tok-a-Tok was the man who actually decided things for the eighteen communities; on 10 October 1867 he struck the Cape South Cape agreement at Niaosong with the Chinese and American parties, and on 28 February 1869 he called on Le Gendre to put the verbal terms into a written memorandum. Among the Qing officials, the Taiwan garrison commander Liu Mingdeng marched five hundred troops as far as the Checheng area, while the circuit intendant Wu Dating and the prefect Yeh Zongyuan stood against the American demands for a battery and for an official station.
kits: 卡面兵器是加特林機槍。理查德·喬登·加特林設計的這種六管速射砲，1860年前後問世、1862年取得專利，槍管環繞中央軸排列，由人力曲柄帶動，每轉一週六管各擊發一次，靠分散後坐與快速換管把射速推到每分鐘數百發，一門需四名射手操作。它在南北戰爭末期由北軍的個人購置者用於彼得斯堡圍城戰役，1866年才正式被美軍採購，美國海軍亦在內戰末期購置「海軍型」三十磅砲裝艦。到1867年6月，這件武器對遠征隊而言仍屬新近列裝的裝備，而本次遠征並沒有加特林砲發射的記載。真正開火的是別的東西：登陸的水兵與海軍陸戰隊員配的是前裝滑膛槍與刺刀，射程短，在叢林裡難以命中；兩艘木殼螺旋槳戰艦靠舊式前裝滑膛艦砲對岸轟擊，清方奏報所記的「花旗國輪船」即指這類蒸汽戰艦；對面排灣族戰士使用的是火槍與長矛，據清方檔案與英方記錄，美軍艦砲的開花彈確實傷到部分原住民戰士。運輸方面，181人靠小艇批次送上岸，艦隊停泊在離岸約半英里的海面，灘頭沒有登陸器材，糧秣主要由艦上供給，因此岸上縱隊一旦深入，回程即成問題。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Gatling gun. This six-barrel rapid-fire gun, designed by Richard Jordan Gatling, appeared around 1860 and was patented in 1862; the barrels revolved around a central shaft turned by a hand crank, each of the six firing once per revolution, and the divided recoil together with rapid barrel rotation pushed the rate of fire to several hundred rounds a minute, with a crew of four serving a single gun. Late in the Civil War, Union officers bought guns with their own money and used them in the trenches at the Siege of Petersburg; only in 1866 was it formally accepted by the US Army, and the Navy likewise bought a Navy Type thirty-pounder for shipboard use late in the war. By June 1867 the weapon was still new equipment as far as this expedition was concerned, and there is no record of any Gatling firing during the campaign. The shooting was done by other things: the sailors and marines who landed carried muzzle-loading smoothbore muskets and bayonets, short in range and hard to hit with in jungle country; the two wooden screw sloops relied on old muzzle-loading smoothbore naval guns to fire at the shore, and the steamships that Chinese officials called wheels and flags in their memorial were precisely such steam warships; the Paiwan warriors on the other side used muskets and spears, and both the Chinese archives and the British accounts record that the American shell splinters did wound a number of the aboriginal fighters. On the logistics side, the 181 men went ashore in boats in successive trips while the squadron lay at anchor about half a mile offshore; there were no landing craft, and food and water came mainly from the ships, so once a column pushed inland the return march was already a problem.
tactics: 美方採用的是十九世紀海軍標準的「艦砲掩護登陸、縱隊深入」套路：兩艦在東南岸外海錨泊，艦砲先行覆蓋灘頭與村落方向，小艇分批把人送上岸，落地即成兩縱隊，貝爾納普一隊、麥肯齊一隊平行前推，隊首由二十名海軍陸戰隊員擔任散兵警戒，全隊目標是「殲滅」排灣族戰士並奪取其村落。這種戰術在熱帶叢林裡很快失靈：美軍官兵穿的是為海上保暖設計的厚重制服，濕熱氣候令行軍士氣崩潰，行軍約六小時後，已有人神智不清或因中暑昏厥。排灣族完全不與美軍正面決戰，而是以游擊方式應對——利用山丘與灌叢的隱蔽位置，以火槍齊射，射完即退，誘使美軍反覆衝鋒然後在叢林裡失去方向；全程美軍未摸到對方一個村子，連一具屍體都沒找到。倒是清廷在事後的處置展示了另一套邏輯：先是依「土牛界線」劃出枋寮至鵝鑾鼻的生番地界，聲稱治權不及而不介入；直到美方態度轉硬，才由劉明燈率兵五百進剿，卻在車城一帶受阻，最後以「安撫為主、設砲臺與設官皆不採」的方式收場。
tacticsEn: The Americans used the standard nineteenth-century naval formula of landing under cover of the ship guns and then pushing columns inland. The two sloops anchored off the south-east coast, the naval guns covered the beach and the direction of the village first, boats ferried the men ashore in batches, and as soon as they were landed the force was split into two parallel columns, Belknap leading one and MacKenzie the other, with twenty marines pushed forward as skirmishers at the head of the line. The declared object was to defeat the Paiwan decisively and capture their village. The formula broke down quickly in tropical jungle: the American officers and men wore heavy uniforms designed to keep them warm at sea, the damp heat drained the column, and after roughly six hours of marching men were already delirious or fainting from heat stroke. The Paiwan never met them in a set-piece action. They fought as a guerrilla force, occupying concealed positions on the hillsides and in the scrub, firing volleys of muskets and then slipping away, drawing the Americans into repeated charges that left them lost in the brush. The Americans never reached a single village and found not a single body. The Qing response, by contrast, followed a logic of its own: a boundary of demarcation drawn from Fangliao to Eluanbi defined the ground as aboriginal and outside the reach of government, and the matter was left alone until American pressure hardened, whereupon Liu Mingdeng was sent in with five hundred men, was checked in the Checheng area, and the affair was closed with conciliation, and with neither the battery nor the official station granted.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下：遠征艦隊兩艘，1867年6月13日在臺灣東南岸外海抵達，錨泊在離岸約半英里處；登陸兵力181名，含海軍軍官、水兵與海軍陸戰隊員，由小艇分批送上岸，岸上推進約六小時；美方損失為一人陣亡，即少校麥肯齊於6月13日當日戰死，另有若干人受傷，重點是多人因高溫中暑神智不清或昏厥而被迫折返；排灣族方面的傷亡極少甚至沒有，美軍搜索後未發現屍體。戰前鋪墊：3月12日羅發號在鵝鑾鼻南方七星岩一帶觸礁，3月26日英軍「鸕鶿」號抵達查證，4月18日李仙得抵臺灣府交涉，五月至六月華盛頓完成決策程序；事後7月25日李仙得隨清兵出發，9月4日抵臺、9月10日劉明燈率兵五百隨行、9月23日抵琅嶠、10月10日在琅嶠立盟、10月23日李仙得返抵廈門，1869年2月28日再會訂立書面備忘錄。武器參數方面：加特林機槍六管、人力轉動、每分鐘約數百發、四人操作；美軍岸上步槍射程與精度都遠不如艦砲，故清方奏報中把艦砲的開花彈與岸上接觸分開記錄。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The expedition consisted of two warships, which arrived off the south-east coast of Taiwan on 13 June 1867 and anchored about half a mile from shore. The landing force of 181 officers, sailors and marines was put ashore in boats in successive trips, and the advance inland lasted about six hours. American losses were one man killed, Lieutenant Commander MacKenzie falling on the day itself, 13 June, together with several wounded; the decisive toll, however, was that several men became delirious or fainted from the heat and had to be turned back. Paiwan casualties were minimal, if any, and the Americans found no bodies. The preliminaries: the Rover struck the reefs off the Seven Stars rocks south of Eluanbi on 12 March; the British HMS Cormorant reached the scene on 26 March to investigate; Le Gendre arrived at the prefectural city of Taiwan on 18 April to press his case; the decision-making in Washington ran through May and June. Afterwards Le Gendre left with the Chinese troops on 25 July, reached Taiwan on 4 September, was followed by Liu Mingdeng with five hundred men on 10 September, reached Niaosong on 23 September, struck the agreement there on 10 October, and Le Gendre was back at Xiamen on 23 October; the written memorandum followed on 28 February 1869. As for the weapons, the Gatling had six barrels, was turned by hand, fired several hundred rounds a minute and needed a crew of four; the muskets carried ashore by the Americans were far shorter in range and far less accurate than the naval guns, which is why the Chinese memorial separates the shell splinters of the ship guns from the fighting on the beach.
cause: 遠征的直接起因是同年三月的一場海難事故，而非任何宣戰。1867年3月9日，美籍三桅帆船羅發號自廣東汕頭開往牛莊，3月12日途經臺灣海峽時被風浪吹偏，在鵝鑾鼻南方七星岩一帶觸礁沉沒；部分船員在獅龜嶺海岸登陸，誤入龜仔甪社範圍，被當地排灣族視為侵略者而遭出草攻擊，僅一人逃到打狗報信。英國皇家海軍「鸕鶿」號3月26日抵達查證後通知美方東印度分艦隊，美國炮艇「阿休埃洛特」號指揮官費比傑隨即由福州赴臺，清廷地方官員卻以生番地界推托，聲稱此次襲擊係不守王化之村落所為，與官府無涉。外交層面，美國駐廈門領事李仙得自4月起嘗試直接與琅嶠十八社聯絡，四月十八日抵達臺灣府仍遭婉拒；清廷不願在生番地帶設官、派兵，也不接受美方提出的保護措施。施壓失效，加上華盛頓內部決策程序耗時三個月，1867年6月，美方決定以小規模懲罰性遠征取代外交交涉，企圖用一次成功的報復迫使清廷改變態度，同時把琅嶠一帶的航路安全問題一次性解決。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of the expedition was a maritime accident in March of the same year, not any declaration of war. On 9 March 1867 the American bark Rover left Shantou in Guangdong for the port of Niuzhuang, and on 12 March, driven off course by wind and sea, she struck the reefs among the Seven Stars rocks south of Eluanbi and went down; part of her crew came ashore on the Shiguiling coast, walked into the territory of the Kulaljuc community, were taken for invaders by the local Paiwan and were killed in a raid, only one man escaping to Takou to give the alarm. The British warship HMS Cormorant reached the area on 26 March, established what had happened and informed the American East India Station; Commander Febiger of the gunboat USS Ashuelot was immediately sent from Fuzhou, but the Qing local authorities passed the buck with a line about the aboriginal frontier, declaring that the raid had been the work of a village that did not respect Chinese law and had nothing to do with the government. At the diplomatic level the American consul at Xiamen, Le Gendre, tried from April to open direct communication with the eighteen communities of Niaosong, and on 18 April he was refused access at the prefectural city of Taiwan; the Qing court was unwilling to set up an official station or station troops in aboriginal territory and would not accept the protection the Americans proposed. With pressure exhausted and the Washington decision procedure eating up three months, in June 1867 the United States decided to replace diplomacy with a small punitive expedition, hoping a successful reprisal would force the Qing court to change its attitude and would settle the question of safe navigation off Niaosong in one stroke.
impact: 這次遠征在美軍戰史上是一次明確的失敗：目標一個都沒達成，卻折損一名少校，成為美國少數幾次海外軍事行動吃敗仗的記錄之一。更深遠的影響落在後續的權力安排上。貝爾等美方軍官在報告中直言，唯一能讓這片海岸真正安全的辦法，是驅走排灣族並把該地置於一個「強大盟友」的管治之下；清廷無力治理生番，李仙得便說服閩浙總督出兵，並接手指揮這支混編隊伍，於1867年10月10日在琅嶠與卓杞篤訂下「南岬之盟」——歸還船長夫婦首級與所劫物品，往後船難者以紅旗為求救信號。清廷官員吳大廷、劉明燈同時否決了美方在象鼻山設砲臺與燈塔的要求，1868年美方提出把琅嶠一帶正式納入版圖、設官駐兵的提案，又屢遭「從緩斟酌」的回覆。事件留下的制度性後果延續甚久：1871年又有琉球船難者被殺事件，1874年日本以「保護琉球人」為名出兵臺灣南部；清廷直到1875年才在鵝鑾鼻建起燈塔，恆春縣城亦因這段糾紛而修築。李仙得因在交涉中取得大量臺灣南部資料，後被日本政府聘為外交顧問，深度介入牡丹社交涉。
impactEn: As a piece of American military history the expedition was an unambiguous failure: not one objective was achieved, yet a lieutenant commander was lost, and it ranks among the few American overseas military operations that ended in defeat. Its deeper consequences lay in the arrangements that followed. Bell and the other American officers stated plainly in their reports that the only way to make that stretch of coast genuinely safe was to drive out the Paiwan and place the area under the control of a powerful ally; the Qing court had no power to administer the aboriginal country, so Le Gendre persuaded the governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang to send troops and himself took command of the mixed column, which on 10 October 1867 concluded the Cape South Cape agreement with Tok-a-Tok at Niaosong: the heads and the goods taken from the captain and his wife were to be returned, and in future a red flag was to be hoisted by shipwrecked sailors as a signal of distress. At the same time Wu Dating and Liu Mingdeng vetoed the American request for a battery and a lighthouse on Elephant Hill, and in 1868 the American proposal to bring the Niaosong area formally under the empire, with an official station and a garrison, was met again and again with the reply to deliberate slowly. The institutional consequences ran for years: in 1871 Ryukyuan sailors were killed after another wreck, and in 1874 Japan sent troops to southern Taiwan under the pretext of protecting them; the Qing court did not build the lighthouse at Eluanbi until 1875, and the walls of Hengchun were raised out of the same wrangle. Because he had gathered a great deal of material on southern Taiwan during the negotiations, Le Gendre was later engaged by the Japanese government as a diplomatic adviser and took a deep part in the settlement of the Mudan incident.
result: 結局是雙方都沒拿到想要的東西。美軍登陸六小時，沒有攻下任何一個村落，沒有擊斃任何一名排灣族戰士，麥肯齊中彈不治，餘部因酷熱中暑而退回艦上，遠征以撤離收場；排灣族方面幾乎無人受傷，隨即退散入山嶺，仍保有對當地的實際控制。清廷的處置則從「不介入」轉為「派兵但不打」：劉明燈率兵五百進至車城一帶即止，最後由吳大廷、李仙得與卓杞篤在琅嶠立約收場，1869年2月28日再以書面形式確認。協議只是一份非正式的諒解備忘錄，不是條約，沒有賠款、沒有割地、沒有建成的砲臺，紅旗求救信號也無人保證會被遵守。事後美方把希望轉向清廷，要求設官、駐兵、建砲臺，得到的卻是拖延；清廷在生番問題上的消極，也為1871年的琉球人遇害事件與其後的牡丹社事件埋下伏筆。對武器史而言，這場遠征則是加特林式速射砲的一次沉默亮相：一件剛進入序列的新式速射武器站在艦上，卻全程沒有發射，真正決定戰局的仍是舊式前裝步槍、艦砲與密林地形。
resultEn: In the end neither side got what it wanted. After six hours ashore the Americans had taken no village, had killed no Paiwan warrior, had lost MacKenzie to a musket ball and had turned back to their ships in the heat; the Paiwan lost virtually nothing, dispersed back into the hills and kept practical control of the ground. The Qing handling shifted from doing nothing to sending troops without fighting: Liu Mingdeng's five hundred men halted in the Checheng area, and the affair was closed by the agreement signed at Niaosong between Wu Dating, Le Gendre and Tok-a-Tok, confirmed in writing on 28 February 1869. The settlement was an informal memorandum of understanding rather than a treaty; there was no indemnity, no cession, no battery actually built, and nobody guaranteed that the red flag would be answered. Afterwards the Americans pinned their hopes on the Qing court, asking for an official station, a garrison and a battery, and got delay in return; the passivity of the Qing on the aboriginal question also laid the groundwork for the killing of Ryukyuans in 1871 and for the Mudan incident that followed. As far as the history of weapons goes, the expedition was a silent debut for the Gatling gun: a new rapid-fire weapon stood aboard the ships having only just entered the inventory, and never fired, and what decided the fighting was still the old muzzle-loading musket, the naval gun and the terrain of the dense forest.
